title: Custom iterables
description: Add `[Symbol.iterator]` to a class or object and it instantly works with `for...of`, spread, and array destructuring.

notes: `[Symbol.iterator]` uses computed-key syntax — the brackets are part of the method name, not array access.
Returning a FRESH iterator each call lets the same iterable be looped multiple times.
Spread, destructuring, `for...of`, `Array.from`, and `Promise.all` ALL use the iterable protocol.

questions.q: What method name makes a class iterable?
Which built-in feature does NOT use the iterable protocol?
questions.explain: `Object.keys` reads own enumerable string keys — it doesn't call `[Symbol.iterator]`.

questions.q: Why return a fresh iterator object from `[Symbol.iterator]()`?
options: Required by the JS spec on every call
So the iterable can be looped multiple times independently
It's not required — returning `this` is identical
